Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden throughput degradation impacting token rates (3/30)

Hi Stephanie —

We observed a sustained degradation in throughput on our production route (model: rw-ggml-v3) between 2028-03-30T08:20:00Z and 2028-03-30T09:05:00Z. During this window our token throughput dropped ~65% and tail latency (p99) spiked to ~6.2s. This caused queued requests to back up and several timeouts on our end.

Can Redwood confirm whether this qualifies as an availability/throughput breach under our agreement and what evidence you need from us for a credit evaluation? We have attached a short packet with our request logs and a top-level timeline.

Attachments: acme_logs_20280330.tar.gz (logs + perf snapshots), p99_latency_snapshot.csv (summary)

Thanks,
Sarah Li
Senior Reliability Engineer
Acme Payments

Thanks Sarah, I pulled the initial SLO calculations for the rw-ggml-v3 pool. Quick summary:
- Policy: 99.9% availability measured as successful token-serving throughput per minute per route.
- Candidate impact window from our telemetry aligns with 2028-03-30T08:18:00Z–2028-03-30T09:07:00Z (ingress drop and autoscaler oscillation observed).
- Observed symptom: autoscaler bounce triggered repeated reshuffling of workers; KV cache misses increased during the window which explains the p99 spike.

Evidence we'll include for credit eligibility:
1) Server ingress/egress traces (per-host)
2) Autoscaler event log and scale-in/out timestamps
3) Kernel-level slowdown artifacts (if any) and agent heartbeats
4) Correlated request ids with your attached logs (please ensure request_id present)

Sarah — can you confirm whether your logs include request_id for a sample of failed/timeouted requests? If not, provide the nearest identifiers/timestamps and we’ll correlate with our traces.

Sarah — thanks for the fast turnaround on the sample ids and timeline. We completed correlation of request_ids to server traces and verified the candidate impact window. Summary:
- Confirmed customer-observed window: 2028-03-30T08:20:00Z–2028-03-30T09:05:00Z
- Root cause (preliminary): rapid scale-in triggered by a mis-tuned transient metric which caused worker churn and cache warm-up penalties. No data exfiltration or integrity issue detected.
- Eligibility: because Acme is on a Reserved (Dedicated) capacity plan with a per-route throughput commitment, this window meets the threshold for an SLA review. We are preparing the credit calculation and will follow the contract Clause 4.2 process.

Next actions:
- Formal evidence bundle (server traces, autoscaler CSV, latency histograms) will be uploaded to the shared drive by EOD 2028-04-03.
- We will schedule a 30-min postmortem call (open to Acme, Redwood SREs, and product) — proposed times: 2028-04-04 10:00–10:30 PT or 2028-04-04 15:00–15:30 PT. Which works for your team?
- Rishi, please draft the customer-facing credit calculation and the note to procurement; include the prorated compensation range per contract.

Rishi — can you take the lead on the compensation note? I’ve attached an internal link to the Jira ticket for context.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Runtime Engineering
Redwood Inference
